name: Question 4
problem: Given the curve $r(t)=⟨2{t}^{2}-t,5-3{t}^{2}⟩,$ find the point at which the tangent to the curve is parallel to the vector $⟨-1,2⟩.$
worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2}-t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5-3{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨4t-1,-6t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $⟨-1\,,\,2⟩$ are parallel for some specific value ${t}_{0}$ of the parameter $t$ if and only if there exists a constant $c$ such that ${r}^{′}({t}_{0})=c⟨-1,2⟩.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =c⟨-1,2⟩ \\ ⟨4t-1,-6t⟩ & =c⟨-1,2⟩ \\ ⟨4t-1,-6t⟩ & =⟨-c,2c⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the components gives:

$$
{\begin{aligned}4t-1=-c \\ -6t=2c\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation, we obtain that $c=-4t+1.$ Substituting $c=-4t+1$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-6t & =2(-4t+1) \\ -6t & =-8t+2 \\ 2t & =2 \\ t & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $⟨-1,2⟩$ and ${r}^{′}$ are parallel only at the point corresponding to $t=1.$

Finally, since

$$
\begin{aligned}r(1) & =⟨2(1)^{2}-1,5-3(1)^{2}⟩=⟨1,2⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

we conclude that $⟨-1,2⟩$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are parallel at the point $(1,2).$

Question 4
?

Given the curve r(t)=⟨2t2−t,5−3t2⟩, find the point at which the tangent to the curve is parallel to the vector ⟨−1,2⟩.

a
(10,−7)
b
(6,−7)
c
(1,2)
d
(0,5)
e
(3,2)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we calculate the derivative of r(t): r′(t)=⟨ddt(2t2−t),ddt(5−3t2)⟩=⟨4t−1,−6t⟩

The vectors r′(t) and ⟨−1,2⟩ are parallel for some specific value t0 of the parameter t if and only if there exists a constant c such that r′(t0)=c⟨−1,2⟩. So, we have

r′(t)=c⟨−1,2⟩⟨4t−1,−6t⟩=c⟨−1,2⟩⟨4t−1,−6t⟩=⟨−c,2c⟩.

Equating the components gives: {4t−1=−c−6t=2c

From the first equation, we obtain that c=−4t+1. Substituting c=−4t+1 into the second equation, we get −6t=2(−4t+1)−6t=−8t+22t=2t=1.

Therefore, ⟨−1,2⟩ and r′ are parallel only at the point corresponding to t=1.

Finally, since r(1)=⟨2(1)2−1,5−3(1)2⟩=⟨1,2⟩, we conclude that ⟨−1,2⟩ and r′(t) are parallel at the point (1,2).
